newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's AC Milan to show 40 bln lire loss - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy's AC Milan to show 40 bln lire loss - paper.

text.p: Italian soccer champions AC Milan, reported to be considering a stock market float, will unveil a loss of 40 billion lire for the financial year ended June 30 plus the months of July and August, financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported on Thursday.
The newspaper said the loss would wipe out the group's entire capital.

Under Milan stock exchange rules, a company wishing to float must show three straight years of profit. AC Milan is owned by billionaire media mogul and opposition Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi.

The club's managing director Adriano Galliani told the daily Corriere della Sera at the weekend that the 1995-96 accounts, due for approval on October 28, would show the club "in the red, heavily in the red". He said Milan could seek to float elsewhere if it proved impossible to do so in Milan.
